items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: McCoy Tyler and Bill Evans, was a beautiful night... they came to see Bill Evans and here they are listening to a Cuban Jazz group

ctx.x: Let’s go back to 78, when Irakere played at Carnegie Hall; what was the response of that audience?

It was very interesting, because that was not announced. When we play in Carnegie hall that was not announced. Probably you can call it the wrong night, because it was a piano night. Mary Lou Williams was playing there, a piano solo; McCoy Tyler and Bill Evans, was a

beautiful night. Piano night was a very quiet night, and then suddenly, eh, Bruce Lundvall came out to the stage and say, “Ladies and Gentleman, we want to give a talking to you. A group—“ blah, blah, blah, and he announced Irakere. “If you want to stay, you can stay, and I think you won’t regret.” So the people stay there, and they have a great time, because they came to see Bill Evans and here they are listening to a Cuban Jazz group that play dance music also.
